title: Admin Canvas: taskifier + simulated dry-run harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Oncall and support engineers have a growing corpus of ad-hoc runbooks and scripts; these are hard to discover, unsafe to run directly, and difficult to measure for regressions. Goal: build an "admin canvas" service + library that turns runbooks into typed, auditable tasks that can be executed via UI, CLI, or API with dry-run and simulated execution modes. The taskifier should emit structured telemetry, require RBAC gating, support idempotent replays, and produce artifacts (logs, replayable step traces, provenance) for post-mortem and quality evals. Scope: - runbook->task compiler (YAML/MD to typed task graph) - safe execution harness (dry-run, simulate, sandbox with synthetic data) - observability hooks (per-step timings, success/failure, token-level cost estimate) - integrations: oncall Slack/GChat actions, console task runner UI, ops CLI; GitHub PRs for changes - security: KMS-encrypted secrets, audit trail, SSO-based consent flow - toggles: canary enablement, A/B rollout with fallback to manual flow Non-goals: rewriting existing runbooks en masse; building a full low-latency streaming runner (this is for interactive operator flows, not bulk repair pipelines).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A CLI command (opsctl canvas compile) converts a representative runbook into a typed task JSON schema and stores it in the task registry
2) UI flow: user can open 'Canvas Task' in Console, step through a simulated dry-run showing step outputs and a synthetic timeline without executing remote side effects
3) Execution: when executed in 'live' mode the task runs under a constrained sandbox with RBAC checks and emits telemetry to /dashboards/tasks and SLO counters
4) Audit: every execution (dry or live) is recorded with a provenance ID and a linkable replay artifact; at least one GitHub PR demonstrates change -> compiled task -> runtime execution flow
5) Security review signoff for KMS handling and consent gating is present in ticket thread
